line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb4+ Bd2
teaches: Blocking a check with a piece that immediately attacks the checking piece turns a defensive move into an offer. The opponent must decide whether to trade off their active bishop or move it a second time, and either answer costs them the tempo the check was supposed to win.
explains: The bishop interposes on d2 and hits the bishop that gave the check. The check has produced nothing, and the piece that gave it now has a decision to make.

line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb4+ Bd2 Nxe4 Nc3
teaches: When a piece takes a central pawn and is not yet safe, the move that wins time is not the recapture — it is the developing move that ATTACKS the piece which took. Recapturing settles the position; developing with a threat keeps the intruder loose, and every move they spend rescuing it is a move you spend bringing another piece out.
explains: The knight comes out to c3 attacking the knight sitting on e4 and covering d5 and b5 on the way. The pawn is not being taken back; the piece that took it is being asked what it intends to do next.
